chunks: Think not that those who exult at what they have done, and who love to be praised for what they have not done, shall escape the punishment, for grievous indeed will be their doom.

key_terms.بِمَا لَمْ يَفْعَلُوا: For what they have not done

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of those who rejoice in what they have done and love to be praised for what they have not done?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the spiritual danger of 'riya' (showing off), where individuals delight in the public perception of their piety rather than the sincerity of their actions before God. It serves as a warning that superficial praise for unperformed or insincere deeds leads to a painful retribution, emphasizing the necessity of inner purity (ikhlas) over external validation.
